messages:
Carla M: FYI customer tenant-123 opened a support ticket — they got a long 429 tail for ~15m, then we saw a sudden flood of previously-blocked requests accepted. looks like limiter refills fired incorrectly :thinking_face:
Ben R: Can you paste the limiter config for that tenant? suspect unit mismatch or a bad deploy.
Carla M: grabbing from prod-config-store, here's the relevant block:
```yaml
limiter:
  refill_amount: 1000
  refill_unit: "minute"  # NOTE: intended to be per-second for burst tenants
  burst: 5000
  algorithm: token_bucket
```
Carla M: kube logs from limiter-host-7 show repeated refills at the minute boundary, but the token counts jumped massively:
```
[INFO] 2026-03-15T12:00:00Z tenant=tenant-123 refill +1000 tokens=6000->7000
[INFO] 2026-03-15T12:00:00Z tenant=tenant-123 refill +1000 tokens=7000->8000
[INFO] 2026-03-15T12:01:00Z tenant=tenant-123 refill +1000 tokens=8000->9000
```
Carla M: The problem is that our runtime interprets `refill_unit` as seconds in most places, but the onboarding UI stored some legacy tenants with "minute". The loader was supposed to convert, but looks like the migration missed this tenant.
Ben R: Ok that explains accepted flood after 429s — stash of tokens got replenished in larger-than-expected chunks. can you repro locally?
Carla M: yes; quick repro script (run from dev box) — hammer endpoint with rate > burst, watch counters: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1","input":"hello"}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
```
Carla M: with the bad config you get 429s initially then after the next refill window a big number of requests succeed (spikes in accepted requests on the metrics).
Dave S: Immediate mitigation: set a short-term override to force per-second refills and lower refill_amount for affected tenants. we should push to admin-api.
Alice K: Agreed. I've got a quick config patch ready to deploy via admin-api. Proposed payload:
```json
{"refill_unit":"second","refill_amount":1,"burst":100}
```
Alice K: Sending to /admin/tenants/tenant-123/limiter now (will gate by canary).
infra-bot: Deploy note: limiter-config service requires hot-reload; restart not required if admin-api sends v2 payload. telemetry will show config.version++.
Ben R: Can we canary to 5% of tenants first? we should avoid mass churn. also add alert: refill_rate_change > 10x.
Carla M: 5% canary sounds good. I'll kick off a targeted rollout and attach the repro harness to watch metrics (requests/429s/accepted). :eyes:
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-089 — TokenBucket refill-unit mismatch — priority P2. runbook assigned to Carla M + Ben R.
Dave S: Post-mortem action items: 1) Add validator on config write to enforce enum for `refill_unit`. 2) Add migration audit to detect tenants with non-standard units. 3) Dashboard: per-tenant refill_delta and active_tokens. 4) Add canary-by-tenant flag for admin-api.
Carla M: I'll own the migration audit and the immediate canary rollout. Ben — can you handle the validator PR? Dave — can you add the dashboard tiles?
Ben R: On it, will open PR with schema validation and unit tests.
Dave S: Adding dashboard card to the ops board now.
Carla M: Closing loop: override applied to tenant-123 at 12:09Z, saw 429s drop to near-zero within one refill window and no new floods. prepping short incident note for support.
Alice K: Thx team. follow-up: schedule a short retro tomorrow to decide whether to run the migration across all legacy tenants or roll a safe conversion patch during low traffic window.
Carla M: +1. also adding a metric-driven alert rule so this doesn't go unnoticed again. :white_check_mark:
